skill.name: linear
skill.description: Manage Linear issues, teams, projects, attachments, and GraphQL workflows through the Linear CLI.
skill.summary: Use Linear CLI workflows to manage issues, projects, comments, links, attachments, and GraphQL queries.
skill.author: 0xBigBoss

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are Markdown formatting or documented Linear CLI examples, not executable malware. Confirmed risks remain around hidden config disclosure or deletion, sensitive /tmp artifacts, broad cleanup, workspace PII enumeration, and an embedded QA prompt that can steer agents.

remediation.suggestion: Move the QA prompt outside the published skill package or mark it as test-only data that agents must not follow during normal use.

remediation.issue: Config file disclosure and destructive reset guidance
remediation.suggestion: Replace direct cat and rm examples for ~/.config/linear/config.json with redacted auth commands and explicit user approval for resets.

remediation.issue: Sensitive or broad use of /tmp paths
remediation.suggestion: Use mktemp or a private directory, clean only exact files created by the workflow, and avoid storing upload responses in predictable paths.

remediation.issue: API key handling examples can leak credentials
remediation.suggestion: Prefer interactive auth or preconfigured environment variables, and warn users not to paste real API keys into prompts, shell history, or screenshots.

remediation.issue: Workspace mutations are documented with confirmation flags
remediation.suggestion: Require agents to show the exact Linear command and receive user approval before creating, updating, linking, deleting, or commenting on issues.

Interacts with Linear for issue tracking and project management using the `linear` command.
- Use for Linear issue/project/teams management via the CLI or GraphQL (`linear gql`).
- Defaults: `linear config set default_team_id TEAM_KEY`, `linear config set default_output json|tab
- Inspect or reset defaults: `linear config show`, `linear config unset default_output`
- **Branches**: Name as `{TICKET}-{short-name}` (e.g., `ENG-123-fix-auth`); prefer git worktrees for
- **Assignment**: Assign yourself when starting work (`linear issue update ENG-123 --assignee me --y
- **Sub-issues**: Set parent to associate related work (requires UUID: `linear issue update ENG-123
- **Scope creep**: Create separate issues for discovered work; link with blocks relation (`linear is
| `linear issues list` | List issues with filters |
| `linear issue view ID` | View single issue |
| `linear issue update ID` | Update issue (assign, state, priority, parent*) |
| `linear issue link ID` | Link issues (blocks, related, duplicate) |
| `linear issue comment ID` | Add comment to issue |
| `linear issue delete ID` | Archive an issue |

*`--parent` requires UUIDs, not identifiers. See [Finding IDs](#finding-ids).
- `--team ID\|KEY` - Specify team (required for most commands)

- [ ] List teams to get TEAM_KEY: `linear teams list`

- [ ] Create child issue: `linear issue create --team KEY --title "Task" --yes`

- [ ] Set parent (UUID required): `linear issue update CHILD_ID --parent PARENT_UUID --yes`
- [ ] Create another issue to link: `linear issue create --team KEY --title "Blocked" --yes`
- [ ] Link blocking issue: `linear issue link ISSUE_ID --blocks OTHER_ID --yes`

content.user_title: Manage Linear Workflows from Your Agent
content.value_statement: Keeping Linear updated from an AI coding session can require many manual context switches. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code CLI workflows for issue, project, attachment, and GraphQL tasks.
actual_capabilities: Lists and searches Linear issues with team, assignee, state, field, and output filters.
Creates, views, updates, comments on, links, and archives Linear issues through CLI recipes.
Lists, creates, views, updates, deletes, and connects Linear projects and issues.
Runs Linear GraphQL recipes for attachments, uploads, relations, assignment, and ID lookup.
Explains authentication, configuration, JSON output paths, common errors, and troubleshooting steps.
limitations: Requires the external Linear CLI package and a valid Linear API key.
Can change real Linear data when commands use confirmation flags.
Raw GraphQL recipes often require UUIDs and current Linear API schema knowledge.
Attachment downloads and upload responses may write files to local paths such as /tmp.

use_cases.title: Manage Assigned Engineering Work
use_cases.description: Review assigned issues, inspect details, add comments, and update state without leaving the coding session.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Project Backlogs
use_cases.description: Create issues, link blockers, organize projects, and keep Linear records aligned with implementation progress.

use_cases.title: Run Linear API Workflows
use_cases.description: Use GraphQL recipes for attachments, file uploads, relations, and bulk ID lookup when CLI commands are not enough.

prompt_templates.title: Show My Linear Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Linear to show my assigned open issues for TEAM_KEY. Ask before changing anything.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Scoped Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Linear issue in TEAM_KEY with this title and description. Show the planned command before running it.

prompt_templates.title: Link Related Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the correct Linear issue identifiers, link ISSUE_A as blocking ISSUE_B, then summarize the resulting relationship.

prompt_templates.title: Run a GraphQL Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Linear GraphQL recipes to find required UUIDs, prepare the mutation, and ask for approval before making changes.

output_examples.input: Show my current Linear work for the engineering team.
output: Assigned issues are grouped by state and priority.
Each issue includes identifier, title, assignee, URL, and next suggested action.
No changes are made without explicit approval.

output_examples.input: Create a task and link it to the blocker I mentioned.
output: The planned issue title, description, team, and relation are shown first.
After approval, the new issue identifier and link relationship are summarized.

output_examples.input: Attach an uploaded design file to a Linear issue.
output: The workflow requests an upload URL, uploads the file, and uses the resulting asset URL.
The final response explains where the attachment was added and how to verify it.

best_practices: Confirm the active workspace, team key, and target issue before running any mutation.
Use built-in CLI commands before raw GraphQL recipes when both options exist.
Keep API keys in the CLI auth flow or environment, not in prompts or shared notes.
anti_patterns: Running commands with confirmation flags before the user approves the exact change.
Pasting real API keys into chat, issue comments, command history, or troubleshooting output.
Reading or deleting the Linear config file when a redacted auth command is sufficient.

faq.question: Does this skill install the Linear CLI?
faq.answer: No. It documents the install command, but the user must approve and perform installation.

faq.question: Can it create and update real Linear issues?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes commands for issue creation, updates, comments, links, and deletion with explicit confirmation.

faq.question: Does it support Linear GraphQL?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes GraphQL recipes for relations, attachments, uploads, assignment, and ID lookup.

faq.question: What credentials are required?
faq.answer: A valid Linear API key is required through the CLI auth flow or an environment variable.

faq.question: Can it download Linear attachments?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents attachment download commands for Linear upload URLs and issue view workflows.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
